original_value: Decision making is the key component of people’s daily life, from choosing a mobile phone to engaging in a war. To model the real world more accurately, probabilistic linguistic term sets (PLTSs) were proposed to manage a situation in which several possible linguistic terms along their corresponding probabilities are considered at the same time. Previously, in linguistic term sets, the probabilities of all linguistic term sets are considered to be equal which is unrealistic. In the process of decision making, due to the vagueness and complexity of real life, an expert usually hesitates and unable to express its opinion in a single term, thus making it difficult to reach a final agreement. To handle real life scenarios of a more complex nature, only membership linguistic decision making is unfruitful; thus, some mechanism is needed to express non-membership linguistic term set to deal with imprecise and uncertain information in more efficient manner. In this article, a novel notion called probabilistic hesitant intuitionistic linguistic term set (PHILTS) is designed, which is composed of membership PLTSs and non-membership PLTSs describing the opinions of decision makers (DMs). In the theme of PHILTS, the probabilities of membership linguistic terms and non-membership linguistic terms are considered to be independent. Then, basic operations, some governing operational laws, the aggregation operators, normalization process and comparison method are studied for PHILTSs. Thereafter, two practical decision making models: aggregation based model and the extended TOPSIS model for PHILTS are designed to classify the alternatives from the best to worst, as an application of PHILTS to multi-attribute group decision making. In the end, a practical problem of real life about the selection of the best alternative is solved to illustrate the applicability and effectiveness of our proposed set and models.

result.paraphrase: Decision making is a key part of everyday life, from selecting a mobile phone to waging war. To represent real-world situations more accurately, probabilistic linguistic term sets (PLTSs) were introduced to handle cases where multiple possible linguistic terms and their associated probabilities are considered simultaneously. In earlier linguistic term sets, all linguistic term sets were assigned equal probabilities, which is unrealistic. During decision making, the vagueness and complexity of real life often leave experts hesitant and unable to state their opinions with a single term, making it hard to reach final agreement. For more complex real-life scenarios, membership linguistic decision making alone is insufficient; a mechanism is needed to express non-membership linguistic term sets in order to deal with imprecise and uncertain information more effectively. In this article, a new concept called probabilistic hesitant intuitionistic linguistic term set (PHILTS) is developed, consisting of membership PLTSs and non-membership PLTSs that describe the opinions of decision makers (DMs). Within PHILTS, the probabilities of membership linguistic terms and non-membership linguistic terms are treated as independent. Basic operations, several operational laws, aggregation operators, a normalization process, and a comparison method are then studied for PHILTSs. Next, two practical decision-making models—an aggregation-based model and an extended TOPSIS model for PHILTS—are designed to rank alternatives from best to worst as an application of PHILTS in multi-attribute group decision making. Finally, a real-life selection problem is solved to demonstrate the applicability and effectiveness of the proposed set and models.
